claim: ntfy publishes via HTTP PUT/POST with five priority levels (1=min to 5=max) set via X-Priority header, tags/emoji via X-Tags, and up to three action buttons (view, http, broadcast, copy).
quote: Priority 5 max/urgent: Really long vibration bursts... Priority 1 min: The notification will be under the fold in 'Other notifications'. Set via X-Priority header. Up to three actions per notification. view, http, broadcast, copy.

claim: ntfy supports attachments up to 15 MB per file (100 MB total per visitor, 3 hour expiry) or external URLs via X-Attach, plus scheduled/delayed delivery via X-Delay (min 10s, max 3 days), click actions, icons, and email publishing.
quote: max 15 MB per file, 100 MB total per visitor, expiry: 3 hours... External URLs: Attach via X-Attach header... Minimum delay: 10 seconds; maximum: 3 days... Email notifications: Set Email header

claim: ntfy provides user/admin roles and ACLs with read-write/read-only/write-only/deny permissions per topic pattern (wildcards supported), access tokens (tk_ prefix, 32 chars), and auth-default-access to make an instance private (deny-all).
quote: read-write (rw)... read-only (read, ro)... write-only (write, wo)... deny (none): neither publishing nor subscribing... auth-default-access... deny-all: Private instance... Tokens must start with tk_ and be 32 characters long.

claim: ntfy acts as a UnifiedPush provider (requires anonymous write-only access to up* prefixed topics), supports browser Web Push via VAPID keys (ntfy webpush keys), and enables near-instant iOS delivery by setting upstream-base-url to forward poll requests to an APNs-connected server.
quote: UnifiedPush requires anonymous write access to the topic... ntfy access '*' 'up*' write-only... Web Push: Enable browser notifications by generating VAPID keypairs (ntfy webpush keys)... iOS Instant Notifications: Set upstream-base-url to forward poll requests to ntfy.sh or another APNS-connected server

claim: Gotify publishes via POST /message?token=<apptoken> requiring only the message field (since v1.2.0), with optional title and priority, and an extras property describing client behavior; it has no native attachment, tag, or action-button support in the core push API.
quote: As of gotify/server v1.2.0 only the message parameter is required... The message API takes an extras property that carries extra information with the message and describes how clients behave to this message

claim: Gotify uses two token types: appToken (applications that send messages) and clientToken (clients that receive messages and manage the server, e.g. the Android app), transmitted via X-Gotify-Key header, token query param, or Bearer Authorization; priority is an integer (default 5).
quote: clientToken (a client is something that receives messages... for example this token should be used for an Android app) and appToken (an application is something that sends messages)... transmitted in a header named X-Gotify-Key, in a query parameter named token or through... Bearer

claim: Apprise is a send-only notification relay (it does not receive notifications) that normalizes to popular services via standardized service://credentials@host/target URLs, with OR/AND tagging, local-file and remote-URL attachments, and YAML/text config files.
quote: Apprise is a send-only notification relay—it does not receive notifications itself... service://credentials@host/target... discord://webhook_id/webhook_token... OR logic: -g devops -g admin... AND logic: -g devops,critical... Attachment Support: Yes... YAML and plain text formats supported

claim: Apprise supports notifications to roughly 143 services (commonly cited as 100+), including Discord, Telegram, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover, email (SMTP), SMS (Twilio/Vonage), Matrix, and Microsoft Teams.
quote: Apprise supports sending notifications to 143 services including email, chat platforms, and SMS providers.

claim: On iOS, ntfy cannot use background WebSocket/JSON-stream connections so all push must traverse APNs; self-hosted servers relay poll requests through ntfy.sh upstream (self-hosted ntfy to ntfy.sh to FCM to APNs to device, then a Notification Service Extension polls back to the self-hosted server for content).
quote: iOS does not allow background processes, so WebSocket or JSON stream connections cannot be used, and Apple requires that all push notifications go through the Apple Push Notification service (APNs)

claim: On iOS 26.2+, ntfy notifications have no sound and a silent ntfy notification can break sound for other apps until a phone call is made, and priority 4/5 Focus/DND bypass is not properly configured in the iOS app.
quote: On iOS 26.2+, ntfy notifications have no sound, and receiving a silent ntfy notification breaks sound for other apps until the user makes a phone call. Priority 4/5 notifications should bypass Focus mode and Do Not Disturb, but the required entitlements... aren't properly configured
